kpis.sub: US BATTERY STORAGE — EIA SEES NEARLY 65 GW BY YEAR-END
kpis.label: EIA's latest tally has operating capacity at nearly 52 GW after 8.3 GW came online in H1 2026, with the agency still projecting 64.9 GW by year-end as another 14 GW arrives in H2 — a further 26 GW is planned for 2027 and 14 GW for 2028, extending the sector's ~70%/year three-year growth run

BNEF still sees 158GW/459GWh of energy storage deployed worldwide in 2026; China supplied roughly 70% of the 18GWh of large-scale BESS that came online globally in July, underscoring how concentrated the build-out remains

kpis.sub: GE VERNOVA BACKLOG — UP 37% YEAR OVER YEAR
kpis.label: GEV's backlog stood at $176B as of Q2, up 37% YoY on AI-data-center and grid-electrification demand, with 2026 guidance now calling for at least 125GW of gas equipment under contract by year-end; shares trade near $946–959 (+37.5% YTD, ~$252B market cap) even after an Aug 27 CFO transition

kpis.sub: EOS ENERGY SURGES ON GOOGLE DATA-CENTER STORAGE DEAL
kpis.label: Eos jumped roughly 19% on Sept 2 after MN8 Energy, Google and Eos unveiled a $350M West Virginia project pairing 86MW of solar with 70MW/280MWh of lithium-ion and 10MW/100MWh of Eos zinc-based (Z3) storage — Google's first use of Eos technology, though storage revenue doesn't begin until 2029–2030

tiers.label: Scale / Revenue-Generating
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Megablock (four 5MWh Megapack 3 units bundled into a 20MWh unit) headlines the roadmap; Q2 deployments hit 13.5 GWh, +41% YoY and the second-largest quarter on record, and a 500MWh Megapack system for Ørsted went live in Texas in early August as the Houston-area Megafactory (targeting 50GWh/yr) nears its own Megapack 3/Megablock production start
rows.watch for: Energy-segment gross margin actually held at 31.4% in Q2 on $1.07B of gross profit — well above the 18% company-wide and 17% automotive margins — the figure to track as Megapack 3/Megablock ramp into Q3/Q4

rows.angle: Global grid-scale leader; Q3 FY26 order intake nearly tripled YoY to a record $1.44B and backlog grew to $6.4B, but roughly $400M of Q3 project deliveries slipped into fiscal 2027 after production issues at a new international contract manufacturer, prompting a FY26 revenue guidance cut to $2.9–3.1B (from $3.2–3.6B)
rows.watch for: Barclays downgraded shares to Underweight on Sept 3 with a $10 price target; the stock fell ~3.9% to $10.36, extending a slide of more than 50% YTD — the demand story (record backlog) keeps losing the argument to the execution story

rows.angle: Grid equipment super-cycle beneficiary; backlog reached $176B in Q2, up 37% YoY on AI-data-center and grid-electrification demand, and the company raised 2026 guidance toward at least 125GW of gas equipment under contract by year-end
rows.watch for: Shares near $946–959 (+37.5% YTD, ~$252B market cap) price in much of the AI-power story; an Aug 27 CFO transition adds a leadership-succession variable alongside the backlog trajectory toward $200B

rows.angle: Pushing past hardware: the agentic AI Assistant remains live inside the Enphase App, IQ Battery C80 commercial pre-orders continue, and Enphase Care — the premium support subscription — passed 7,500 US enrollments (announced Sept 1)
rows.watch for: Sell-side consensus has settled at Hold (19 analysts, as of Sept 2) with shares trading $34.82–$36.21 — the residential-solar policy headwind (net-metering phase-outs abroad, US policy uncertainty) remains the dominant swing factor, not product cadence

tiers.label: Next-Gen / Speculative
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Solid-state lithium-metal batteries (VW-backed); Cobra-process QSE-5 cells continue shipping to Volkswagen Group and were demonstrated on the Ducati V21L race bike; the Honda R&D/manufacturing partnership and the Eagle Line pilot keep running toward a scaled-manufacturing blueprint
rows.watch for: No fresh catalysts since the July Q2 print and June Honda agreement; Truist's price target still sits at $6 (cut from $8) and the Street's median near $7.50 masks a wide $2.50–$10 dispersion, with still no production license, no volume commitment, and no revenue

rows.angle: Zinc-based long-duration storage (LDES); Sept 2 news of a $350M multi-technology project with Google and MN8 Energy in West Virginia (86MW solar, 70MW/280MWh Li-ion, 10MW/100MWh Eos Z3) marks Google's first use of Eos tech and the state's first commercial LDES deployment — shares jumped ~19% on the news
rows.watch for: Storage revenue doesn't start until 2029–2030, so this validates the technology and lengthens the logo list without changing near-term financials; the Q2 net loss that widened to $275.7M and the securities-law investigations opened Aug 20 remain unresolved, and the Thorn Hill manufacturing consolidation's 10–15% conversion-cost cut still doesn't arrive until 2027

rows.angle: AI-driven storage optimization software (PowerTrack); Q2 2026 (reported Aug 12) EPS of -$1.58 beat the -$1.99 estimate, and FY26 revenue guidance was reaffirmed at $140–190M
rows.watch for: No fresh catalysts this week; Roth Capital's Aug 17 cut to $6.75 from $11 still stands since the reaffirmed guide sits below the $158M Street consensus at the midpoint — cost control is working, top-line conviction still isn't there

rows.angle: Battery/gravity storage integrator; the 1.25 GW off-grid BESS + grid-forming power deal for a hyperscale Texas data center (~$500–600M of expected 2H26–2027 revenue) remains the headline proof point
rows.watch for: Still facing direct competition for data-center BESS deals after Cummins' Aug 18 announcement of its largest-ever BESS deployment for an undisclosed US data center — the co-located storage niche keeps getting crowded by larger, better-capitalized players

bear_case.title: China dominates cells — and keeps adding cost levers
bear_case.description: China's domestic power-battery installations hit 76.5GWh in June alone (+31.5% YoY), with CATL holding 42.7% share and BYD 18.5%; both are now exporting that scale advantage abroad — BYD's 11.275GWh Masdar (Abu Dhabi) storage win and a new CATL-Alfen supply deal bringing 5GWh of sodium-ion batteries to Europe show the pattern spreading beyond home turf. CATL's Naxtra sodium-ion cells remain on track for cost parity with LFP by year-end, with first China deliveries of the TENER Sodium grid system beginning this month — a cost-curve threat layered on top of existing scale dominance.

bear_case.title: Tariffs and policy add a second axis of pressure
bear_case.description: Section 301 tariffs on Chinese-origin battery energy storage systems rose to 25% on January 1, 2026, pushing the combined tariff burden on Chinese batteries and BESS to roughly 55%, while FEOC content thresholds now disqualify projects leaning too heavily on restricted foreign entities — starting at 55% in 2026 and tightening to 75% after 2029. Wood Mackenzie still projects an 11% contraction in the US utility-scale storage market in 2026 (and a further 8% decline in 2027) even as EIA data shows capacity still climbing toward 64.9GW by year-end — compliance costs are rising regardless of which growth trajectory proves right.

bear_case.title: Margin compression
bear_case.description: Barclays downgraded Fluence to Underweight on Sept 3 with a $10 price target, and shares fell to roughly $10.36 — a fresh sign that the ~$400M of Q3 deliveries pushed into fiscal 2027 on contract-manufacturer delays is a durable concern, not a one-quarter blip, even against a record $6.4B backlog. Eos Energy's Sept 2 Google/MN8 partnership is a genuine technology and logo win, but it generates no storage revenue until 2029–2030 and does nothing for the Q2 net loss that widened to $275.7M or the open securities-law investigations — the sector keeps proving it can win orders faster than it can convert them to margin.

bear_case.title: Solid-state timelines
bear_case.description: QuantumScape has gone quiet since its July Q2 print and June Honda R&D agreement — no September catalysts have emerged, and Truist's $6 price target (cut from $8 in August) still stands against a Street range of $2.50–$10. The absence of news is itself a data point: with no production license, no volume commitment, and no revenue, the gap between demonstrated lab performance and mass-manufacturable solid-state cells sits exactly where it was a month ago.
